blocks.text: Wizards of the Coast has now officially confirmed the 2027 booster changes, including God Packs and Japan Showcase cards in the Booster Pack wildcard slot.

Wizards of the Coast announced on October 5 that Play Boosters and Collector Boosters will change beginning with the first Magic: The Gathering set of 2027, Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, according to the Wizards Play Network retailer page and Magic's official announcement. God Packs will appear in the packs, and Japan Showcase cards will move into Booster Packs.

A God Pack contains five foil Booster Fun rare and/or mythic rare cards, and Wizards says one in every 300 Collector Boosters will hold one. StarCityGames reports the same Collector Booster rate alongside a Booster Pack rate of one in every 1,000. Wizards said the additions meant finding room in its printing capacity.

Japan Showcase cards, previously exclusive to Collector Boosters, can now appear in the wildcard slot of Booster Packs in traditional foil. MTG Rocks reports that the change also makes Collector Boosters smaller and describes it as the biggest change to the Booster Pack formula in years. The Wizards Play Network recommends stores walk their staff through the new Booster Pack name and contents and decide how they will handle God Packs during events.

records.headline: Wizards of the Coast Confirms God Packs and 2027 Magic Booster Changes
records.dek: The changes begin with Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, the first Magic set of 2027, and bring Japan Showcase cards to the wildcard slot of Play Boosters.

blocks.text: Update — Wizards of the Coast has now published its own announcement, 'Updating Our Boosters in 2027', on the official Magic site, confirming God Packs and the wider booster changes for the first set of 2027.

Wizards of the Coast is changing what Magic: The Gathering players find inside Play Boosters and Collector Boosters, starting with Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, the first set of 2027. The company confirmed the changes in its own announcement, 'Updating Our Boosters in 2027', published on its official site on 5 October.

God Packs headline the update, according to Draftsim, which describes it as the first major booster change since Play Boosters arrived in 2024. Draftsim reports a Play Booster God Pack in 1 of every 1,000 boosters, and SSBCrack describes a God Pack as holding only rare or mythic rare cards. For Collector Boosters the rate is 1 in every 300, a figure that appears in both Draftsim's report and Wizards' announcement.

Other changes arrive with the same set. A foil card opened in a Booster Pack will be a rare or mythic rare, and the announcement describes a 'foil fancy slot' filled by five Foil Booster Fun rare or mythic rare cards. Japan Showcase cards, previously the domain of Collector Boosters, can be opened in the wildcard slot of Play Boosters in traditional foil. Wizards says the additions needed room in its printing capacity.
Draftsim reports that Universes Beyond sets in 2027, including Star Trek, will not be affected by the changes.

Kotaku's report describes the Collector Booster God Pack as containing 14 cards, while Wizards' announcement states the rate of 1 in every 300 Collector Boosters. The difference has not been resolved.

blocks.text: Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek releases on November 13, 2026, and preorders are open now. The official Magic: The Gathering site confirmed the date and the preorder window on October 20, in a buyer's guide published alongside a mechanics overview and a collecting guide.

Preorders run through local game stores, TCGplayer, Amazon and other retailers that sell Magic. The buyer's guide sets out the contents of the Draft Night product, while the collecting guide lists the Collector's Edition Commander Deck at $159.99 and 30 stardates cards.

items.text: Release date: November 13, 2026, with preorders open at local game stores, TCGplayer, Amazon and elsewhere Magic is sold.
Each Draft Night includes 12 Play Boosters, a Collector Booster, and a collection of tokens and basic lands.
Collector's Edition Commander Deck: $159.99.
The set contains 30 stardates cards, per the collecting guide.
MagicCon: Atlanta and World Championship 32 run November 13–15.

blocks.text: Preorders are open ahead of release day, so the practical question for players is which product to order; the Draft Night contents are spelled out at 12 Play Boosters plus a Collector Booster. For collectors, the 30 stardates cards give a defined subset to track from launch.
